title: Keeping support while releasing its form

captions.energy: Holding to familiar models of care

meaning: Your domestic support keeps its meaning when ending a familiar form allows care to find a present expression suited to both.
text: You can support one another at home through a method that once helped greatly but no longer fits. The Star in the physical position of Muladhara preserves the wish to share support and hope. The Hierophant in energy holds to a familiar model as the only correct one, while Death in emotions experiences the need to end what is outdated. This creates a difficult gap: you want to remain dependable for each other, yet changing care’s form seems to question its earlier value and sincerity.

For example, cooking together in the evening once helped you feel at home. Timetables have now changed, and waiting for each other every day leaves both hungry and tired. **Releasing an earlier form does not mean giving up support itself.** Leaving dinner ready can preserve care better than compulsory meetings at the cooker. The past does not become a mistake because today’s arrangements require another way of participating.

The difficulty is continuing custom to prove faithfulness or, exhausted, dismissing everything earlier altogether. Both responses obscure the intention that remains. Support grows when an ending concerns a specific form rather than the right to rely on one another. You can then acknowledge what the previous arrangement offered without forcing it to work in circumstances it no longer suits.
